newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends up with firmer cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends up with firmer cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures, driven by Wednesday's bullish inventory data and firmer physical prices, ended with modest gains Thursday, but prices remained in recent technical ranges, sources said.
August climbed 2.7 cents to close at $2.175 per million British thermal units. September settled 2.5 cents higher at $2.118. Others deferreds ended up 0.8 to 2.5 cents.

"Cash was strong this morning and the AGAs certainly didn't give any reason to sell it. We're still stuck in a range, but if cash doesn't break soon, we're going to see some convergence by paper," said one Midwest trader, noting the seven cent cash premium to futures with just three days left before August goes off the board.
AGA said Wednesday that U.S. gas stocks rose last week by 58 bcf, well below average estimates in the 75-80 bcf range.

While most agreed catch up storage buying after last week's record heat and production cuts from Hurricane Danny helped boost the physical market this week, few expected the rally to carry far with little extreme weather ahead.
Temperatures in the Midwest and Northeast are forecast to briefly warm by the weekend but more seasonal weather is expected by early next week.
Chart traders agreed August was range bound, but said the wide spread between cash and futures kept the bears cautious.

August support was seen at $2.07 and then at the $2.051 low from July 8. Major trendline resistance this week was in the $2.21 area, with further resistance pegged at the $2.29 and $2.36 prominent highs.
In the cash Thursday, Gulf Coast prices firmed four cents to the low-$2.20s. Midcon pipes were up about a nickel to the mid-teens. New York city gate gas firmed a few cents to the low-to-mid $2.40s.
The NYMEX Henry Hub 12-month strip gained 1.7 cents to $2.218. NYMEX volume figures were not available.

On the KCBT, August finished up 3.5 cents at $2.10, while deferreds ended one to three cents higher. The East/West spread narrowed by 0.8 cent to 7.5 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 243 lots traded, down sharply from Wednesday's total of 492.
